//: Policy for what an agent may do THROUGH an MCP server. Enforced by .claude/hooks/guard-mcp.mjs on Cursor's beforeMCPExecution and Claude Code's PreToolUse. Hand-edited on purpose - this is a policy, not a generated artifact.
//why: Two locks already exist and both are somebody else's to keep: the github server's X-MCP-Readonly header, and postgres-mcp's --access-mode=restricted. .mcp.json says it plainly - the access mode is defence in depth, not the boundary. Drop a header, point at a role with more grants, add a server on a Friday, and the lock is gone with nothing in this repo objecting. This is the lock that lives with the code and fails the build.
//unlisted: A server nobody wrote a policy for is allowed, and reported. Denying by default sounds stricter and is worse: the first unlisted server breaks the workspace, someone disables the hook, and every server becomes unlisted.

github.//write: Mirrors X-MCP-Readonly on the server. Reads, searches and listings pass; anything that changes a repo does not.
github.//deny: Denied even if someone sets write:true. Merging a PR and force-pushing are not 'writes' in the ordinary sense - they are the two operations no review can undo.
github.//phases: Opening a PR during REQUIREMENTS or DESIGN means code exists that the design gate never approved. NOTE: dormant while write is false - create_pull_request is denied as a write before the phase is ever consulted. That is the strictest rule winning, which is correct, but do not read this line as active governance until someone sets write:true.

postgres.//sqlAllow: The leading keyword of any sql/query/statement argument must be one of these. postgres-mcp's own read-only mode was bypassed once by a SQL-injection flaw in its predecessor; this checks the statement the agent actually sent.

context7.//: Documentation lookups. Nothing it returns should ever be executed unread, but nothing it does can change state either.

playwright.//write: It drives a browser; that is the whole point. The risk here is not mutation but reach - a browser can log into things. Keep it off for backend-only sessions, as .mcp.json already advises.
